name: IELTS Writing Task 2 Vocabulary
description: Từ và cụm từ học thuật cốt lõi cho IELTS Writing Task 2: lập luận, nguyên nhân, hệ quả, giải pháp, chính sách, xã hội, kinh tế, sức khỏe và môi trường. Bộ được thiết kế theo nhu cầu Lexical Resource và Coherence/Cohesion.

words.example: Many people argue that public transport should be subsidised.
words.note: Use to introduce a position or line of reasoning.

words.example: Some commentators assert that technology improves productivity.
words.note: More formal than say or claim.

words.example: Critics contend that the policy would increase inequality.
words.note: Formal academic alternative to argue.

words.example: The government claims that the reform will reduce costs.
words.note: Use carefully when presenting a claim that may need evidence.

words.mean: cho rằng; duy trì quan điểm
words.example: Supporters maintain that the measure is necessary.
words.note: Formal way to describe a sustained position.

words.example: The evidence suggests that early education has long-term benefits.
words.note: Useful for cautious academic claims.

words.example: The findings imply that demand may continue to rise.
words.note: Stronger than suggest but still indirect.

words.example: Recent research indicates a link between sleep and concentration.
words.note: Common academic verb for evidence.

words.example: The study demonstrates the value of regular exercise.
words.note: Use when evidence clearly supports a point.

words.example: The report highlights the risks of excessive screen time.
words.note: Useful for introducing an important issue.

words.example: Experts emphasize the importance of preventive healthcare.
words.note: Formal spelling is emphasize in American English and emphasise in British English.

words.example: It is important to acknowledge the disadvantages of the proposal.
words.note: Useful for presenting a balanced argument.

words.example: Some researchers challenge the assumption that bigger schools are better.
words.note: Useful for discussing opposing evidence or views.

words.mean: biện minh; chứng minh là hợp lý
words.example: Governments should justify major increases in public spending.
words.note: Useful when discussing reasons for a policy or decision.

words.example: Many experts advocate stricter controls on air pollution.
words.note: Common in formal discussions of policy.

words.example: Residents opposed the construction of a new airport.
words.note: Useful for presenting disagreement with a proposal.

words.mean: lợi ích; mang lại lợi ích
words.example: One major benefit is improved access to healthcare.
words.note: Common collocation: benefit from, mutual benefit.

words.example: A major drawback is the cost of implementation.
words.note: Useful alternative to disadvantage.

words.example: One possible consequence is increased pressure on housing.
words.note: Common collocations include serious, unintended, and long-term consequences.

words.example: The decision has significant implications for young workers.
words.note: Useful for discussing wider effects of an issue.

words.example: Building more cycle lanes is a feasible solution.
words.note: Use for ideas or plans that can realistically be implemented.

words.mean: khả thi; có thể duy trì
words.example: The proposal is financially viable in the long term.
words.note: Useful for practical and economic feasibility.

words.example: Cities need more sustainable forms of transport.
words.note: A core word for environment, development, and policy topics.

words.example: Excessive stress can be detrimental to mental well-being.
words.note: Formal alternative to harmful.

words.example: Regular exercise is beneficial for both physical and mental health.
words.note: Formal alternative to helpful or good for.

words.example: Obesity is prevalent in many developed countries.
words.note: Useful for describing a widespread problem.

words.example: The use of facial recognition remains controversial.
words.note: Useful for topics with divided public opinion.

words.example: The report presents compelling evidence for the reform.
words.note: Use for strong reasons or evidence.

words.mean: then chốt; cực kỳ quan trọng
words.example: Access to clean water is crucial to public health.
words.note: Formal alternative to very important.

words.example: The policy could have a significant economic impact.
words.note: Useful for both scale and importance.

words.example: Some level of change may be inevitable in a growing city.
words.note: Useful when discussing unavoidable outcomes.

words.example: Governments can mitigate the effects of climate change.
words.note: Formal verb for reducing harm or severity.

words.example: Better public services could alleviate pressure on hospitals.
words.note: Useful for reducing a problem rather than eliminating it.

words.example: Poor planning can exacerbate traffic congestion.
words.note: Strong formal alternative to make worse.

words.example: Authorities must tackle the causes of youth unemployment.
words.note: Common with social and environmental problems.

words.example: The policy aims to address inequality in access to education.
words.note: Extremely useful for formal essays.

words.example: Higher taxes may curb excessive consumption.
words.note: Useful for reducing undesirable behaviour or trends.

words.example: Schools can foster creativity and independent thinking.
words.note: Common with innovation, skills, cooperation, and development.

words.example: Governments should promote healthier lifestyles.
words.note: Common policy verb with health, education, and sustainability.

words.example: Financial incentives can encourage companies to recycle.
words.note: Useful for policies that aim to change behaviour positively.

words.example: Higher fines may deter people from breaking the law.
words.note: Useful for crime and regulation topics.

words.mean: điều tiết; quản lý bằng quy định
words.example: Governments need to regulate online advertising aimed at children.
words.note: Common in technology, business, health, and environmental essays.

words.example: Authorities may impose stricter limits on emissions.
words.note: Common collocations include impose a tax, ban, fine, or restriction.

words.example: Governments should allocate more funds to public healthcare.
words.note: Common with resources, budgets, and funding.

words.example: Cities should invest in reliable public transport.
words.note: Common with money, infrastructure, education, and technology.

words.example: Governments could subsidise renewable energy projects.
words.note: British spelling used in IELTS contexts; American spelling is subsidize.

words.example: Policy makers should prioritise preventive healthcare.
words.note: British spelling used in IELTS contexts; American spelling is prioritize.

words.example: The government should implement the reform gradually.
words.note: Common with policy, strategy, measure, and programme.

words.example: Authorities must enforce environmental regulations consistently.
words.note: Useful when discussing laws and compliance.

words.example: New legislation could improve workplace safety.
words.note: Useful for formal discussion of legal measures.

words.example: The policy aims to reduce household energy use.
words.note: Core word for government action.

words.example: Modern infrastructure is essential for economic growth.
words.note: Common with transport, digital networks, and utilities.

words.example: Income inequality remains a major social issue.
words.note: Often paired with reduce, widen, address, or tackle.

words.example: Improving accessibility to higher education should be a priority.
words.note: Useful for education, healthcare, transport, and services.

words.example: Housing affordability is a serious concern for young adults.
words.note: Common in housing, healthcare, and education discussions.

words.example: Flexible working can improve employee productivity.
words.note: Useful for work, technology, and economic topics.

words.example: Technological innovation can transform many industries.
words.note: Common in technology, education, and business essays.

words.mean: việc làm; tình trạng có việc làm
words.example: The project could create employment in rural areas.
words.note: Useful economic noun for jobs and labour topics.

words.example: Excessive consumption puts pressure on natural resources.
words.note: Common with energy, water, food, and goods.

words.example: The exploitation of natural resources can damage ecosystems.
words.note: Useful in environmental and social justice contexts.

words.example: Stronger laws are needed to prevent discrimination in the workplace.
words.note: Common collocations include racial, gender, and age discrimination.

words.example: Public awareness of healthy eating has increased.
words.note: Common with raise, increase, improve, and public awareness.

words.mean: khả năng phục hồi; sức chống chịu
words.example: Communities need resilience in the face of natural disasters.
words.note: Useful for climate, society, and personal development topics.

words.mean: hạnh phúc; sức khỏe tổng thể
words.example: Urban planning should support residents' well-being.
words.note: Useful for health, work, education, and quality-of-life topics.

words.example: Preventive medicine can improve public health.
words.note: High-value phrase for health policy essays.

words.example: Education can contribute to long-term economic growth.
words.note: Useful for economy and development topics.

words.example: Inclusive education can strengthen social cohesion.
words.note: Useful for multiculturalism, inequality, and community topics.

words.example: Reliable public transport can improve quality of life.
words.note: Useful for evaluating broader social outcomes.

words.example: The policy requires a long-term strategy.
words.note: Common with effects, solution, investment, and planning.

words.example: Short-term savings should not undermine long-term benefits.
words.note: Useful for evaluating trade-offs.

words.example: Policy decisions should be evidence-based.
words.note: Useful for formal recommendations and public policy arguments.

words.mean: tiết kiệm chi phí; hiệu quả về chi phí
words.example: Improving bus networks can be a cost-effective measure.
words.note: Useful for comparing policy options.

words.example: Governments should encourage environmentally friendly transport.
words.note: Useful for environmental solutions.

words.example: Rapid reform can create unintended consequences.
words.note: Useful for balanced discussion of policies.

words.example: Schools play a role in shaping healthy habits.
words.note: Flexible phrase for discussing causes and influences.

words.example: Air pollution poses a serious threat to public health.
words.note: Useful for discussing risks.

words.example: Population growth can exert pressure on housing supply.
words.note: Useful for cause-and-effect arguments.

words.example: The proposal is effective in terms of cost and accessibility.
words.note: Useful for precise comparison of criteria.

words.example: From my perspective, public transport should be prioritised.
words.note: Useful for opinion essays; keep use limited and natural.

words.example: To a large extent, technology has changed how people work.
words.note: Useful for nuanced agreement or partial evaluation.
